title: Edge kernel profiling brain dump — morning run
content:
Morning notes 

Goal: isolate what caused a 2x jump in 99p token latency on the edge pool between 03/08 and 03/09. Quick hypothesis: kernel scheduling + small-batch locking contention when KV cache miss spikes. Secondary: new memcpy change from PR #2184 interacting with NUMA placement.

What I ran (local repro):
- small harness: ./bench --model rwd-7b --seq 1024 --concurrency 3 --batch-size 1 --warmup 30 --duration 120
- observed baseline on my devbox (A100 80GB): p50 ~11ms, p95 ~26ms, p99 ~48ms (weird: p99 fluctuates)
- with emulated KV-cache churn (random prefix invalidation): p99 jumps to ~95ms, CPU steal increases on server 2

Collected traces/logs:
- kernel traces: see snippet below from perf script (trimmed):
  2026-03-09T09:12:08Z sched_wakeup: pid=2431 comm=worker tid=2431 cpu=2
  2026-03-09T09:12:08Z sched_switch: prev=worker next=worker2 latency=278us
  2026-03-09T09:12:08Z futex_wait: pid=2431 addr=0x7f2b8c0fdc40
  repeated futex contended ~200x in 1s window

- strace on runtime: heavy futex_wait time when KV miss path executed (blocked for 800–1200us per call)
- memcpy trace: recent libtorch upgrade added a conditional fast-path that does non-temporal stores for >4KB copies; triggering on our per-token tensor ops?

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
1) Futex contention in the per-request scheduler lock during KV cache refill. Reproduce by increasing NVMe latency (tc qdisc) and see futex counts.
2) NUMA imbalance: worker pinned to wrong node causing costly cross-node memcpy leading to stall under tail load.
3) New memcpy path in lib introduced false sharing or clflush patterns that slow down small copies when many threads active.

Quick next steps (today):
- [ ] Add perf counters in runtime around KV cache miss path (measure time spent in lock vs IO). TODO: instrument kv_cache.cpp, log microseconds per-futex attempt. Owner: me. ETA: today EOD.
- [ ] Reproduce with tc qdisc to simulate NVMe 5–10ms spikes and see p99 correlation. Command: sudo tc qdisc add dev nvme0 root netem delay 8ms 2ms distribution normal
- [ ] Run same harness with GDB/rr on a single worker to capture the exact instruction where thread park happens. Might be slow but useful.
- [ ] Try disabling the memcpy fast-path (set env RW_MEMCPY_FAST=0) and re-run 1h harness. If p99 goes down -> memcpy root cause.
- [ ] Check kernel version matrix on edge pool (reported mix of 5.10 and 6.1). If older kernel has a scheduler regression for heavy futex users. Diego to ping infra.

Notes from short chat with Mina: she saw increased page-faults on edge nodes (minor) and suggested checking for madvise/hugepage behavior. I should try running with MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0 and see if glibc brk behavior affects latency.

Quick experiment results (03/11):
- Disabling memcpy fast-path reduced p99 by ~18% under artificial KV churn but not enough to account for 2x jump.
- tc qdisc delay reproduced p99 increases with markedly more futex stalls. Strong signal for IO-triggered contention.

Longer-term ideas:
- Move KV cache refill off the hot path: background refill + optimistic read with epoch counters to avoid holding central lock. (Sketch: per-worker refill queue, single refill thread per socket)
- Convert some per-request locks to seqlock/RW lock to reduce contention for readers
- Explore kernel patched futex wake batching (if exists) or lock-free queues for short critical sections

Open questions / debugging tips:
- Why only edge pool? Possibly denser allocation (higher concurrency per machine) + older kernel + smaller instance types. Check instance types and packing policy.
- Are any autoscaling events correlated? Need to cross-check with console logs for 03/08–03/09.

Short TODO mapping to tickets (to create):
- Create SERV-XXXX: instrument kv cache (me)
- Create SERV-XXXX: run NUMA/pack tests (infra + me)
- Create SERV-XXXX: optmize memcpy path / vendor follow-up (runtime + applied-ml)

Housekeeping:
- Slack thread: #runtime-ops, drop inline logs and link to GH#2184 for memcpy note.
- If I can't repro locally by EOD, escalate to oncall for a live-run on edge cluster next week.

Random quick commands I used: 
- sudo perf record -a -g -- ./bench ...
- perf script | ./annotate-fw 
- sudo tc qdisc add dev nvme0 root netem delay 8ms 2ms
- sudo taskset -c 0-7 ./bench ...

End-of-day quick summary (12 Mar): made progress narrowing to I/O-triggered futex contention; memcpy helps but not the primary; next: instrument + run isolated edge instance repro.

Notes to self: keep log snippets small; append full compressed traces to GH ticket.
